narrative:
The model estimates a 68% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expected to stay.

The strongest influence came from the fact that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with higher turnover risk, as it suggests you have viable alternatives that could pull you away.

Your six to ten years of experience in this organization worked in the opposite direction. This tenure is longer than what most employees predicted to stay typically have, and it slightly pulled the prediction toward staying by showing you have built some roots here.

Your overall career experience of six to ten years also pushed the prediction toward leaving. While this level of experience is fairly common, it still contributed to the model seeing you as someone with enough market value to potentially move on.

Taken together, the pull from external opportunities outweighed the stabilizing effect of your time with the company. The organization should discuss with you how to address the appeal of outside offers, perhaps through clearer career progression or targeted retention steps. You may want to reflect on whether those opportunities better match your long-term goals.
